source.title: News Letter, 22 October 1993, p. 2 ("Voters spurn Tories (Cumming 234 first preferences; Coates won by 24 on second count)"); Irish News, 22 October 1993, p. 7 ("Alliance takes North Down seat"); Belfast Telegraph, 20 October 1993, p. 4 ("Preview: North Down voters go to the polls today (five-candidate line-up with labels)"); Belfast Telegraph, 21 October 1993, p. 6 ("Alliance takes council seat (count-day story)"); Belfast Telegraph, 26 August 1993, p. 5 ("Election day: special council meeting voted for a by-election after failing to agree unanimously on co-option")
source.publisher: News Letter / Irish News / Belfast Telegraph (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: No full count found. ARK percentages: United Unionist 34%, Alliance 34%, Ind [Swimming Pool] 22%, Cons 10%, Ind [Action '93] 1%; Cumming's 234 at 10% implies a valid poll of roughly 2,300-2,500 (not recorded). Poll day: BT of Wed 20 Oct says voting today and result Thursday lunchtime; News Letter of Fri 22 Oct speaks of 'yesterday's' by-election, meaning the count.

note: By-election of 20 October 1993 for one seat in Holywood (North Down), caused by the resignation of Dr Laurence Kennedy (Conservative), 27 July 1993, over the Conservative-UUP understanding at Westminster; council failed to agree unanimously on co-option (special meeting late August 1993). The reports found give the result but not every candidate's votes, so no figures are shown.

countGroup.Party_Basis: Printed 'Unionist'; ARK files him as United Unionist, a DUP candidate with UUP support
